title: Incident boot sculptor and PD thread orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: When high-severity traces surface (latency spikes / error storms) our on-call flow still requires multiple manual steps: creating a dedicated Slack incident thread, attaching a minimal evidence bundle (trace snippets, top error logs, sample spans), linking the PagerDuty incident and inserting a templated runbook. This manual stitching costs precious minutes during P0s and leads to inconsistent postmortem artifacts.

Goal: Implement an 'incident boot sculptor' service that automates initial incident thread creation and a 'PD thread orchestrator' that wires PD incidents, Slack threads, and runbook templates together. The feature should reduce time-to-first-action for on-call responders, ensure consistent evidence attachments, and seed a postmortem draft in the background.

Scope:
- Trigger points: SLO breach alerts, tracing-sampled anomaly detector, and manual PD alerts with metadata.
- Create Slack incident thread with consistent naming, pinned checklist, and buttons for common actions (acknowledge, escalate, open war room).
- Attach curated evidence bundle: top 5 error traces, latency histogram slice, related logs link, and a minimal KV cache snapshot where applicable.
- Link to PagerDuty incident and add PD quickactions in thread (add priority, reroute).
- Seed a postmortem Markdown draft in Confluence (or internal drive) with initial timeline and evidence attach links.
- Provide operator-facing controls in Console to toggle auto-seed, evidence sensitivity levels, and template selection.

Non-goals: full automated remediation or replacement of existing PD escalation policies. This is orchestration and seeding only.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- Evidence sensitivity: conservative default to avoid PII leakage. We will use sampled spans and redaction filters described in the privacy policy doc. Ops can opt into expanded bundles for trusted incidents.
- Slack vs. other chat: initial rollout to Slack only (majority of teams). MS Teams support will be scoped later.
- Attachment storage: store evidence bundles in short-lived signed URLs (48h) rather than uploading large payloads to Slack to avoid quotas.
- Idempotency: incidents may be re-triggered. Sculptor must detect existing threads/attachments and dedupe to avoid spamming on-call channels.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument tracing hooks to surface annotated span groups (signal IDs) that the sculptor will query.
2) Build evidence bundler service responsible for fetching traces/log slices, applying redaction, creating signed bundle artifacts.
3) Develop PD thread orchestrator that listens to PD webhooks and creates/updates Slack threads + attaches bundle links.
4) Console controls and feature flags for per-org opt-in and sensitivity selection.
5) Seed postmortem drafts via Confluence API and attach links to the Slack thread.
6) Integration tests and staged rollout to a pilot org.

Links / artifacts:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Boot+Sculptor+Spec
- Evidence bundler prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8421
- Console feature flag prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1902

Operational concerns:
- Rate limiting: avoid creating threads for noisy low-value alerts; use enrichment score threshold.
- Observability: instrument sculptor metrics (created_threads_total, dedup_hits, bundle_generation_latency_ms, bundle_size_bytes) and traces for each orchestration path.
- Rollback: feature flag must support immediate disable per org and a global kill switch.
acceptance_criteria: Given a P0 SLO breach alert with trace signal id, the system auto-creates a Slack incident thread in the configured ops channel within 30s
The thread contains a pinned starter checklist, a link to an evidence bundle with signed URL (valid 48h), and a button to open a war room
PagerDuty incidents created/updated include a back-reference to the Slack thread; interacting with PD quickactions updates the Slack thread status
A postmortem draft is created in Confluence with initial timeline entries and evidence links when auto-seed is enabled
Console shows a per-org toggle and sensitivity level control; toggling off prevents new auto-created threads for that org
Evidence bundles are redacted according to the privacy filter; no raw PII/log lines are present in the bundle by default
End-to-end integration tests pass in staging and pilot rollout (sample org) for at least two incident types (latency spike, error flood)
